# Class-4-CPU latency table (protocol compliance, not a performance claim)

> CPU-only measurement on AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M with 8 threads; not comparable to published GPU latency or throughput figures.

timer `time.perf_counter_ns`, sync `ort_run_blocking`, 10 warm-ups, 5 repeats; threads 8 on AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M. p95 is indicative at 5 samples; read the median and the min/max/IQR.

| X shape | backend | median ns | p95 ns | min ns | max ns | IQR ns | samples | threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (4, 64) | `onnx-fp32-matmul` | 8200 | 8960 | 7700 | 9100 | 700 | 5 | 8 |
| (4, 64) | `onnx-int4-matmulnbits` | 14200 | 14480 | 13900 | 14500 | 400 | 5 | 8 |
| (4, 64) | `onnx-int8-matmulinteger` | 13600 | 15000 | 13000 | 15300 | 600 | 5 | 8 |
| (512, 64) | `onnx-fp32-matmul` | 15800 | 20700 | 15200 | 21900 | 300 | 5 | 8 |
| (512, 64) | `onnx-int4-matmulnbits` | 46600 | 47280 | 45700 | 47400 | 900 | 5 | 8 |
| (512, 64) | `onnx-int8-matmulinteger` | 22500 | 23020 | 22400 | 23100 | 300 | 5 | 8 |

**No speedup is claimed or implied.** At these shapes the absolute latency is dominated by ONNX Runtime session-call overhead, so the table's value is protocol compliance: it shows the kernels execute our containers under a controlled, disclosed protocol with a same-session fp32 baseline.
